name: Matbench: highest phonon DOS peak frequency
description: Predict the frequency (cm^-1) of the highest-frequency peak of the phonon density of states of 1265 crystals from their structure. The evaluator scores the mean absolute error over Matbench's five official cross-validation folds.

sources.locator: Legrain et al. (2017): predicting vibrational free energies and entropies of solids from composition with machine learning.
Petretto et al. (2018): high-throughput DFPT phonon calculations for inorganic materials; source of the targets.
Dunn et al. (2020): Matbench v0.1 tasks, nested cross-validation protocol and MAE metric.
matbench_v0.1_validation.json (official folds) and stored per-fold predictions of published submissions (pinned commit).
Per-task Matbench v0.1 leaderboard (mean MAE over the five folds).

requirements.datasets: matbench_phonons with the official folds. Fetched by python3 scripts/prepare_chemistry.py from pinned sources and verified by SHA-256 (catalog/chemistry-data-lock.json); not redistributed.

evaluation.benchmark: Matbench: highest phonon DOS peak frequency
evaluation.paper_metric: Local protocol; see candidate contract and source adaptation notes

execution.interface: fit_predict(train_inputs, train_targets, test_inputs, info) -> list of len(test_inputs) floats. Inputs are ordered crystal structures {'lattice': 3x3 lattice vectors as rows (Angstrom), 'species': element symbols, 'frac_coords': fractional coordinates per site}. Called once per official Matbench v0.1 fold (five calls, KFold(5, shuffle, random_state=18012019)), each in a fresh process that receives that fold's training inputs with targets and its held-out inputs without targets; info = {'task', 'input_type', 'target', 'unit', 'fold', 'n_train', 'n_test'}. Runs in a separate process that receives only these arguments (no test values), with at most 4 threads (OMP/MKL/OpenBLAS set to 4), no network, no subprocesses and no read access to the repository or prepared data; numpy, scipy, scikit-learn and RDKit are importable (pandas and torch only where the environment provides them; they are not requirements of the task); wall-clock limit 170 s per fold. Score: mean over the five folds of the held-out mean absolute error in target units (minimize), the Matbench leaderboard metric

limitations: All targets are public in the Matbench files and every sample is a test sample of one fold; candidates or settings tuned on these folds overfit, so treat scores as development scores.

Leaderboard entries were trained without this task's limits (170 s and at most 4 CPU threads per fold, CPU only), so leaderboard values are reference points rather than targets attainable under the same budget.
Targets are harmonic DFPT results, not measurements, for compounds within 150 meV of the convex hull; 1265 samples.

Candidates run in a separate process that never receives held-out values, but the process isolation is an audit-hook policy for honest program search, not a security boundary (ctypes stays available for scientific libraries); run adversarial evaluations in a container.

state_of_the_art.statement: Best mean MAE on the Matbench v0.1 leaderboard for matbench_phonons: 28.7606 cm^-1 (MegNet (kgcnn v2.1.0)), read on 2026-10-10.

science_relevance.scientific_problem: Predict lattice vibrational properties (the highest phonon density-of-states peak) of crystals from their structure.
science_relevance.importance_rationale: Phonons determine thermal conductivity, heat capacity and phase stability; DFPT calculations are expensive, so learned predictors speed up screening for thermal and thermoelectric materials.
